column3: The Hebrew locates the ark in the “field of the Philistines”; BSB renders this as their “land.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew describes knowledge passively as something that “will be known to you”; BSB uses active “you will understand.” It says the hand does not “turn away” from them, rendered “has not been lifted” in BSB.
The Hebrew leaves the questioning speakers unnamed; BSB identifies them as the Philistines.
The Hebrew repeats “images” for the rats and calls them “your rats”; BSB leaves both implicit. It says God may make His hand light upon them, where BSB says He may “lift His hand.”
The Hebrew uses singular “your heart” and “their heart”; BSB uses plural “your hearts” and the implicit plural “theirs.”

The Hebrew says the yoke has not “gone up upon” the cows and commands bringing their young home from behind them. BSB renders these as having “never been yoked” and taking the calves away to pen them up.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the responsible one as “he”; BSB explicitly supplies the LORD. The hand is described as having “touched us,” rendered “punished us” in BSB.
The Hebrew explicitly says the calves were confined “in the house”; BSB simply says “penned up.”
The Hebrew lists the chest, the gold rats, and the tumor images with repeated “and”; BSB explicitly presents the latter objects as contents of the chest.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they lifted their eyes and rejoiced to see the ark; BSB uses “looked up” and “were overjoyed.”

The Hebrew says the cart stopped there and that a large stone was there, using two separate clauses. BSB combines them as stopping “near a large rock” and supplies “the people” as the ones chopping the cart.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists the cities and repeats “one” for each gold tumor; BSB combines them under “one gold tumor for each city.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew lists “seventy men, fifty thousand men”; BSB states only “seventy men.” The Hebrew leaves the initial striking subject unnamed; BSB supplies God.
The Hebrew leaves the one to go up unnamed; BSB explicitly supplies “the ark.”
The Hebrew says to bring it up “to you”; BSB renders this as taking it up “with you.”
